text:
emily: Pushed a docs PR to tighten up SDK snippets for streaming + pagination across py/ts/go. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/578. Goals: use empty-string as canonical cursor start, show per-call deadlines, and add a tiny knob cheat for ops. Can folks quick-review?
peter: quick skim. good move to normalize cursor. one ask: can we show both AbortController (TS) and an explicit small-batch pattern? helps with backpressure examples.
hao: agree. for Python prefer `async for` + `asyncio.wait_for` for per-call deadline. keep examples minimal.
sara: go snippet should show `context.WithTimeout` and demonstrate passing a resume token header. also add a 1-line migration note for v1 users.
emily: added examples accordingly. TS snippet uses AbortController and stops after N tokens: ```ts
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = client.responses.stream({model: 'redwood-mini', input: q, signal: ac.signal});
let seen = 0;
for await (const chunk of stream) { handle(chunk); if (++seen >= 30) ac.abort(); }
```
peter: nice. also include an alternate TS pattern showing small batch reads (read batches of 8) for throughput/latency tradeoff.
emily: added that too. Python snippet now: ```py
async def consume(q):
  async for part in client.responses.stream(model='redwood-mini', input=q):
    process(part)
await asyncio.wait_for(consume(q), timeout=0.25)
```
hao: Go snippet: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 250*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req.Headers.Set("x-resume-token", token) // token may be empty string for first page
stream, err := client.StreamResponses(ctx, req)
for stream.Next() { ev := stream.Event(); handle(ev) }
```
sara: one docs nit: older examples used `null` in some places. please normalize to `""` and add a short note: "Use \"\" to request the first page; server returns an opaque resume token for subsequent pages."
emily: done. also added a 1-paragraph migration note under the snippet section (v1 -> v2 snippet change: cursor default).
peter: small inline "knob cheat" under examples (one line each): batching -> throughput ↑ ; small per-call deadlines -> bounded latency ; TTL cache -> fewer cold starts. keep it inline, not a new page.
sara: added a tiny FAQ: "Why is my resume token long?" Answer: opaque (often base64), don't parse it; pass it back to `cursor` as-is.
docs-bot: PR 578 updated: snippet smoke-tests passed and docs linter green.
emily: planning to merge in 20 unless any objections. will follow release-bot and open a follow-up if users ask for more migration examples. :shipit:
